newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farm officials disagree on hop reform aid.
newsitem.headline: Farm officials disagree on hop reform aid.

text.p: Disagreement has surfaced over aid levels for hop producers, the key element in a proposed reform of European Union hop marketing rules, EU diplomats said.

They said that the Special Committee on Agriculture, which discussed the issue in Middelburg this week, objected to a European Commission plan to phase in a single area aid hop premium over five years to replace payments for aromatic and bitter varieties.
Germany and other producer countries are seeking aid of 600 ecus a hectare whereas the Commission envisages a level of only 450 ecus.
They argue that aid should be increased following a fall in world prices due to increased production outside the EU.
The Commission also wants to allocate five percent of aid to encourage producers to switch to more marketable varieties.
Germany also wants aid to promote hop research and development.
EU hop subsidies cost only about 14 million ecus a year.
Germany is the main producer, accounting for 80 percent of the EU hop area of some 27,650 hectares. Britain is the second most important of the EU's eight hop producing countries.
Diplomats were optimistic that the SCA, which will discuss hop reform again next week, will settle the issue without having to send it to ministers.
